en: The *Mukundamālā* composed by King Śrī Kulaśekhara:
I bow to Mukunda, whose eyes are as broad as the petals of a lotus, whose teeth are like jasmine, the moon, and a conch shell, who wears the dress of a young cowherd;
I praise the son of Vasudeva, whose footstool is worshipped by hosts of gods beginning with Indra, and whose abode is Vṛndāvana. (KMuk_1)

Victory, victory to this god, the delight of Devakī! Victory, victory to Kṛṣṇa, the lamp of the Vṛṣṇi lineage! Victory, victory to him who is dark as a rain-cloud and possesses tender limbs! Victory, victory to Mukunda, the destroyer of the earth’s burden! KMuk_2 //
Having prostrated with my head before Mukunda, I entreat you for this one exclusive favor:
by your grace, may there be no forgetting of your lotus-feet in birth after birth.
The honey from the lotus feet of the glorious Mukunda is most wonderful:
those who drink it are not deluded, while those who do not drink it are deluded.
O Hari, I do not worship the pair of your feet for the sake of attaining freedom from duality, nor to remove even the heavy hellish torment of Kumbhīpāka;
nor do I desire to sport with beautiful women of tender limbs in the Nandana grove. In every state of being, within the palace of my heart, I meditate upon you alone.

I have no attachment to the Dharma, nor to the accumulation of wealth, nor indeed to the enjoyment of sensual pleasures; O Blessed One, let whatever is destined to happen occur in accordance with my past karma.
This alone is my great aspiration: may unwavering devotion to the pair of your lotus-feet persist for me, even throughout future births.
Whether my dwelling be in heaven, on earth, in hell, or even beyond the end of hell as I desire—
yet at the moment of death, I shall think only of your feet, which have disregarded the autumnal lotuses.
O mind, do not cease from sporting here with the lotus-eyed Murāri, who holds the conch and the discus;
I know of no other source of happiness that is ever equal to the nectar of remembering the feet of Hari.
Do not fear, O dull-witted one; having reflected in many ways, know that these long-lasting torments do not prevail over us, for our Lord is indeed Śrīdhara.
Casting off laziness, meditate upon Nārāyaṇa, who is easily attained through devotion; is He, the remover of the world's calamities, not capable of helping His servant? (KMuk_9)
"Do not let your heart fall into despondency, thinking, 'How shall I cross this unfathomable and difficult-to-traverse ocean of existence?
Your singular devotion, fixed upon the lotus-eyed Lord who destroys hell, will surely carry you across."

O Giver of Boons, O Abode of the Three, be gracious toward us who are sinking in the great ocean called saṃsāra—an ocean where craving is the water, delusion is a series of waves tossed by the wind of passion, the cycle of existence is a whirlpool, and it is teeming with a multitude of crocodiles that are our own sons; grant us the boat of devotion to Your lotus feet.
A particle of dust is but an atom; water is mere droplets; fire is a feeble spark; the wind is a faint breath; space is a most subtle void;

and all the gods, from Rudra and Pitāmaha down to the lowliest, are but insects—wherein [all these] are seen as such, may that Lord of Yours, for whom the cycle of worldly existence ends in liberation, be victorious upon the earth.
The study of the Vedas is like weeping in a forest; daily observances of arduous vows are merely steps toward cutting away fat; all rites of public charity are like pouring oblations into ashes;
and plunging into sacred fords is like an elephant’s bath—except for the praise of his two lotus-feet. Victorious is that Lord Nārāyaṇa!
"Ānanda, Govinda, Mukunda, Rāma, Nārāyaṇa, Ananta, Nirāmaya"—though capable of uttering these names, no one speaks them; alas, such is the worldly affliction of people regarding liberation!
Salutations to Mādhava, the enemy of Madhu, whose beautiful form is starred by the spray from the waves of the milk-ocean, and who reclines upon the couch of the serpent’s coils.

Because of His affection, because of His commitment to granting fearlessness, because of His dispelling of the suffering of the distressed, because of His magnanimity, because of His drying up of sins, and because of His bestowing of countless states of supreme bliss—the Lord of Śrī alone is to be served by all the world with absolute devotion; of this, Prahlāda, Vibhīṣaṇa, Airāvata, Draupadī, Ahalyā, and Dhruva are witnesses.

While the Lord Śrī Puruṣottama—the sole sovereign of the three worlds, the one to be served with the mind, the supreme Nārāyaṇa who bestows his own station—remains present, alas, we fools and wretches search for some base man, a mere lord of a few villages who gives little wealth, for the sake of service! KMuk_17 //
O people, listen! Those sages who know yoga, such as Yājñavalkya and others, proclaim this remedy for the disease of birth and death:
let the one, immeasurable, immortal light within, called Kṛṣṇa, be drunk; for when that supreme medicine is drunk, it bestows ultimate liberation.

O Lotus-eyed One, may our lives always be fulfilled for us who constantly taste the nectar of meditating upon the pair of your lotus feet—with joined palms, with bowed heads, with limbs bristling with horripilation, with throats choked by emotion, and with eyes shedding streams of tears. (KMuk 19)

O tongue, as you utter words that express the supreme reality beyond all else—words that, as it were, drip with nectar—turn back toward the names that have Nārāyaṇa as their object; I stand before you with palms joined in reverence.
This body, delicate by its very nature, will inevitably fall apart with its joints loosened and worn out;
why do you weary yourself with medicines, O fool of evil mind? Drink the disease-free elixir of Kṛṣṇa!
Having uttered the glorious name known as Nārāyaṇa, even sinners have obtained their desires;
alas for us, our speech did not previously proceed toward it, and therefore we have experienced the sufferings of dwelling in the womb and so forth.

May I never, even for a moment, behold those whose merit is exhausted and who are devoid of devotion to Your lotus feet; may I never hear Your life-story, so well-suited to be heard, having cast aside all other collections of tales;
may I never touch You, O Mādhava, Lord of the World, with a mind that denies You; and may I never be deprived of the practice of Your worship, even in birth after birth.
O Madana, you have become emaciated by the fire of Śiva’s eye while occupying a place in my mind that is the abode of Mukunda’s lotus feet;
do you not remember the prowess of Murāri’s discus?
The daughter of the excellent ocean is your wife; this Viriñca is your son; the Veda is your hymn of praise; the host of gods is your circle of servants;
liberation is your favor; the entire world is within you; Devakī is your mother; and the son of Balaripu is your friend in truth—I know nothing else in reality.
O tongue, proclaim Keśava; O mind, take refuge in Śrīdhara, the enemy of Mura; O pair of hands, worship the stories of Acyuta; O pair of ears, listen!
O pair of eyes, look upon Kṛṣṇa; O feet, go to the abode of Hari’s feet; O nose, smell the *tulasī* from Mukunda’s feet; and O head, bow down to Ādhokṣaja!
That head alone is auspicious which is whitened by the dust from prostrating before Kṛṣṇa; those eyes are truly beautiful when they behold Hari, freed from the darkness [of ignorance].
That intellect is pure through its observances and restraints which meditates upon Mādhava; that tongue rains down nectar at every step which praises Nārāyaṇa. (KMuk 27)

May the crest-jewel of the cowherds—the jewel that is Garuḍa to the serpents of those who hate his devotees, the jewel that protects the three worlds, the jewel that is a cloud to the cātaka-birds of the Gopīs’ eyes, the jewel that is the seal of beauty, the jewel that is the beloved Śrī Rukmiṇī, the unique jewel that adorns the pair of Urvashi-like breasts of the dark-complexioned one, and the crest-jewel upon the peak of what is to be meditated upon for the sake of supreme welfare—grant us prosperity. 28. KMuk_28 //

O tongue, constantly chant, chant the mantra of Śrī Kṛṣṇa— the sole mantra for the destruction of enemies, the mantra honored by all the sentences of the Upaniṣads, the mantra that delivers one from saṃsāra, the mantra for the liberation of those with disciplined minds, the sole mantra for all sovereignty, the mantra that protects from being bitten by the serpent of calamity, and the mantra that makes birth fruitful.

O mind, drink the medicine of the name of Śrī Kṛṣṇa— the medicine that eradicates delusion, the medicine for the activity of the sages' mental states, the medicine that destroys the misfortunes of the Daityas, the sole medicine that revives the three worlds, the medicine that pacifies the suffering of devotees, the divine medicine that annihilates the fear of worldly existence, and the medicine that brings about the attainment of the highest good.
This is indeed a marvel in the world of men: they abandon the nectar and drink poison;
abandoning the names that fall within the domain of Nārāyaṇa, these deceivers recite other words.

Foolish poets spend their days describing the eyes of Lāṭī women, the jars of their breasts, the banks of the Revā river, and the dense thickets of sandalwood trees; meanwhile, for those men whose minds are fixed solely on Him, time passes away in utterances of "Govinda," "Janārdana," "Lord of the Worlds," and "Kṛṣṇa."

I possess this very provision for my journey from here: the fortune of the nectar of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s name, which is not to be begged for, not to be bought, not stale, not to be cooked, inexhaustible, and easy to carry.

This hymn was composed by King Kulaśekhara, who, like a bee at the lotus-feet of the Lotus-eyed One, had two beloved friends—Śruta and Dhara—who were celebrated throughout the world of poets and were auspicious to the circle of the twice-born. KMuk_34 //
Thus ends the *Mukundamālā*, composed by King Kulaśekhara.
